text: How many legs does a spider have?
explanation: Spiders are arachnids and have eight legs.

text: How many hours are there in one day?
explanation: A day is divided into 24 hours.

text: Which ancient civilization built the Great Pyramids of Giza?
explanation: The pyramids of Giza were built by the ancient Egyptians about 4,500 years ago.

text: What did the Wright brothers famously fly for the first time in 1903?
explanation: In 1903 the Wright brothers made the first controlled, powered airplane flight.

text: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
explanation: The Pacific is the largest and deepest of Earth's oceans.

text: Which is the coldest continent on Earth?
explanation: Antarctica is the coldest continent, covered almost entirely by ice.

text: Which planet do humans live on?
explanation: Humans live on Earth, the third planet from the Sun.

text: What is the common name for H2O?
explanation: H2O, two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom, is water.

text: Which animal is often called the "King of the Jungle"?
explanation: The lion is traditionally nicknamed the King of the Jungle.

text: What color are the leaves of most plants in summer?
explanation: Most leaves are green because of the pigment chlorophyll.

text: In the classic fairy tale, which girl loses a glass slipper at the royal ball?
explanation: Cinderella leaves behind a glass slipper as she rushes from the ball.

text: Who wrote the play "Romeo and Juliet"?
explanation: "Romeo and Juliet" was written by William Shakespeare.

text: Which famous portrait by Leonardo da Vinci is known for its mysterious smile?
explanation: Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa is famous for her enigmatic smile.

text: Which color do you get by mixing blue and yellow paint?
explanation: Mixing blue and yellow paint makes green.

text: How many strings does a standard acoustic guitar have?
explanation: A standard guitar has six strings.

text: Which of these instruments has black and white keys?
explanation: The piano is played using a keyboard of black and white keys.

text: What is the name of the lion cub hero of Disney's "The Lion King"?
explanation: Simba is the young lion who becomes king in "The Lion King".

text: What kind of animal is Disney's flying character Dumbo?
explanation: Dumbo is a baby elephant who can fly using his big ears.

text: In which sport can a player perform a "slam dunk"?
explanation: A slam dunk is a basketball shot forced down through the hoop.

text: How often are the Summer Olympic Games normally held?
explanation: The Summer Olympics are normally held every four years.

text: Which key is usually the longest on a computer keyboard?
explanation: The space bar is the longest key on a standard keyboard.

text: What does "www" stand for in website addresses?
explanation: "www" stands for World Wide Web.

text: Which fruit is long, curved and yellow when ripe?
explanation: A ripe banana is long, curved and yellow.

text: Which sweet food is made by bees?
explanation: Bees make honey from the nectar of flowers.

text: In Greek mythology, who is the king of the gods?
explanation: Zeus rules the gods from Mount Olympus in Greek mythology.

text: Which mythical creature looks like a horse with a single horn on its forehead?
explanation: The unicorn is a legendary horse with one horn on its forehead.

text: How many letters are in the English alphabet?
explanation: The English alphabet has 26 letters, from A to Z.

text: Which word is the opposite of "hot"?
explanation: "Cold" is the opposite of "hot".

text: What is the name of Nintendo's famous mustached plumber?
explanation: Mario is Nintendo's mustached plumber mascot.

text: Which toy brand is famous for its colorful interlocking plastic bricks?
explanation: LEGO is known worldwide for its interlocking plastic bricks.

text: How many sides does a hexagon have?
explanation: A hexagon is a polygon with six sides.

text: How many zeros are there in one million written as a number?
explanation: One million is written 1,000,000, with six zeros.

text: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon first, in July 1969.

text: The Great Wall, built over many centuries, is located mainly in which country?
explanation: The Great Wall stretches across northern China.

text: What is the capital city of Japan?
explanation: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.

text: What is the longest river in Africa?
explanation: The Nile is the longest river in Africa.

text: At what temperature does water boil at sea level?
explanation: At sea-level pressure, water boils at 100 °C.

text: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
explanation: Mars looks red because of iron oxide on its surface.

text: What is the largest animal that has ever lived on Earth?
explanation: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived.

text: What is a young frog that lives in water and has a tail called?
explanation: A tadpole is the aquatic larval stage of a frog.

text: Which young wizard attends Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry?
explanation: Harry Potter is a student at Hogwarts in J. K. Rowling's novels.

text: Which author created the detective Sherlock Holmes?
explanation: Sherlock Holmes was created by Arthur Conan Doyle.

text: Who painted "The Starry Night"?
explanation: Vincent van Gogh painted "The Starry Night" in 1889.

text: What are the three primary colors in traditional painting?
explanation: In traditional color theory, red, yellow and blue are the primary colors.

text: Which composer wrote the famous "Ode to Joy" melody in his Ninth Symphony?
explanation: "Ode to Joy" is the finale of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony.

text: How many musicians play in a quartet?
explanation: A quartet is a group of four musicians.

text: In which film series do Jedi Knights fight with lightsabers?
explanation: Jedi Knights and lightsabers come from the Star Wars saga.

text: What is the name of the cowboy doll in Pixar's "Toy Story"?
explanation: Woody is the cowboy doll who leads Andy's toys in "Toy Story".

text: How many players does each football (soccer) team have on the field at once?
explanation: Each football team fields eleven players, including the goalkeeper.

text: In which sport does the word "love" mean a score of zero?
explanation: In tennis, a score of zero is called "love".

text: Which company makes the iPhone?
explanation: The iPhone is designed and sold by Apple.

text: Which symbol appears in every email address?
explanation: Every email address uses the @ symbol between the user name and domain.

text: What is the main ingredient of guacamole?
explanation: Guacamole is a Mexican dip made mainly from mashed avocado.

text: Sushi is a traditional dish from which country?
explanation: Sushi is a traditional Japanese dish of vinegared rice.

text: Which hero of Greek mythology had to complete twelve labors?
explanation: Heracles, called Hercules by the Romans, performed the Twelve Labors.

text: In Norse mythology, which god wields the hammer Mjölnir?
explanation: Mjölnir is the hammer of Thor, the Norse god of thunder.

text: What is a word that has the same meaning as another word called?
explanation: A synonym is a word with the same or nearly the same meaning as another.

text: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
explanation: Mandarin Chinese has more native speakers than any other language.

text: Which round yellow arcade character eats dots while avoiding ghosts?
explanation: Pac-Man eats dots in a maze while being chased by ghosts.

text: Pikachu is the mascot of which famous Japanese franchise?
explanation: Pikachu is the best-known character of the Pokémon franchise.

text: Which Roman numeral represents the number 50?
explanation: In Roman numerals, L stands for 50.

text: What is the sum of the interior angles of any triangle?
explanation: The interior angles of a triangle always add up to 180°.

text: Whose expedition completed the first circumnavigation of the Earth, in 1519–1522?
explanation: Ferdinand Magellan's expedition made the first voyage around the world.

text: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World stood in Alexandria, Egypt?
explanation: The Lighthouse of Alexandria, or Pharos, was one of the Seven Wonders.

text: What is the capital city of Australia?
explanation: Canberra is the capital of Australia.

text: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
explanation: Vatican City, at about 0.44 km², is the world's smallest country.

text: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
explanation: Gold's symbol Au comes from its Latin name, aurum.

text: How many bones are in the typical adult human body?
explanation: A typical adult human skeleton has 206 bones.

text: What is the fastest land animal?
explanation: The cheetah can sprint at around 100 km/h, faster than any other land animal.

text: How many hearts does an octopus have?
explanation: An octopus has three hearts: two pump blood to the gills and one to the body.

text: Who wrote the novel "Don Quixote"?
explanation: "Don Quixote" was written by the Spanish author Miguel de Cervantes.

text: Which Russian author wrote "War and Peace"?
explanation: "War and Peace" is a novel by Leo Tolstoy.

text: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
explanation: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling between 1508 and 1512.

text: Together with Georges Braque, which artist pioneered Cubism?
explanation: Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque developed Cubism in the early 1900s.

text: Which composer wrote the set of violin concertos "The Four Seasons"?
explanation: "The Four Seasons" was composed by Antonio Vivaldi.

text: How many keys does a standard modern piano have?
explanation: A standard modern piano has 88 keys: 52 white and 36 black.

text: Who directed the 1993 film "Jurassic Park"?
explanation: "Jurassic Park" was directed by Steven Spielberg.

text: Which animation studio produced the 2001 film "Spirited Away"?
explanation: "Spirited Away" was made by Studio Ghibli and directed by Hayao Miyazaki.

text: How many interlocking rings appear on the Olympic flag?
explanation: The Olympic flag shows five interlocking rings.

text: Which sport is the Tour de France?
explanation: The Tour de France is a multi-stage road cycling race.

text: In computing, what does "CPU" stand for?
explanation: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit.

text: Who invented the World Wide Web?
explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 at CERN.

text: Paella is a traditional rice dish from which country?
explanation: Paella comes from Valencia, Spain.

text: Which spice is made from the dried stigmas of a crocus flower?
explanation: Saffron consists of the dried stigmas of the saffron crocus.

text: In Greek mythology, who flew too close to the Sun on wings of feathers and wax?
explanation: Icarus flew too near the Sun, which melted the wax of his wings.

text: Which ancient Egyptian god is usually shown with the head of a jackal?
explanation: Anubis, god of mummification, is depicted with a jackal's head.

text: What do you call a word or phrase that reads the same backward as forward?
explanation: A palindrome reads the same in both directions.

text: From which language does the word "kindergarten" come?
explanation: "Kindergarten" is German for "children's garden".

text: In which country was the Rubik's Cube invented?
explanation: The Rubik's Cube was invented in 1974 by Hungarian architect Ernő Rubik.

text: In which country was the video game Tetris originally created?
explanation: Tetris was created by Alexey Pajitnov in Moscow, Soviet Union, in 1984.

text: Which number does the Roman numeral MCM represent?
explanation: MCM is 1000 (M) plus 900 (CM), which equals 1900.

text: How many faces does a regular icosahedron have?
explanation: A regular icosahedron has 20 triangular faces.

text: Mansa Musa, often called one of the richest people in history, ruled which empire?
explanation: Mansa Musa ruled the Mali Empire in the 14th century.

text: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
explanation: Marie Curie shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics, the first won by a woman.

text: What is the deepest lake in the world?
explanation: Lake Baikal in Siberia is about 1,640 m deep, the deepest lake on Earth.

text: Which is the driest non-polar desert in the world?
explanation: The Atacama Desert in Chile is the driest non-polar desert.

text: Which gas makes up the largest share of Earth's atmosphere?
explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere.

text: What is the chemical symbol for tungsten?
explanation: Tungsten's symbol W comes from its other name, wolfram.

text: Which living bird has the largest wingspan?
explanation: The wandering albatross has the largest wingspan of any living bird, up to about 3.5 m.

text: How many compartments does a cow's stomach have?
explanation: A cow's stomach has four compartments: rumen, reticulum, omasum and abomasum.

text: Who wrote the novel "One Hundred Years of Solitude"?
explanation: "One Hundred Years of Solitude" was written by Colombian author Gabriel García Márquez.

text: In which language did Dante originally write "The Divine Comedy"?
explanation: Dante wrote "The Divine Comedy" in Italian (Tuscan) rather than Latin.

text: Which artist painted "The Persistence of Memory", with its melting clocks?
explanation: Salvador Dalí painted "The Persistence of Memory" in 1931.

text: In which city is the Prado Museum located?
explanation: The Museo del Prado is in Madrid, Spain.

text: Which composer wrote the opera "The Magic Flute"?
explanation: "The Magic Flute" was composed by Mozart in 1791.

text: How many lines make up a standard musical staff?
explanation: A standard musical staff has five lines.

text: What was the first feature-length film made entirely with computer animation?
explanation: Pixar's "Toy Story" (1995) was the first fully computer-animated feature film.

text: Which director made the classic films "Rashomon" and "Seven Samurai"?
explanation: Both films were directed by Akira Kurosawa.

text: In which city were the first modern Olympic Games held in 1896?
explanation: The first modern Olympics took place in Athens, Greece, in 1896.

text: What is the official distance of a marathon race?
explanation: A marathon is officially 42.195 km long.

text: What does "HTML" stand for?
explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language.

text: Which programming language was created by Guido van Rossum?
explanation: Guido van Rossum created Python, first released in 1991.

text: Which type of pasta is shaped like large grains of rice?
explanation: Orzo is a small pasta shaped like grains of rice.

text: Which nut is the main ingredient of marzipan?
explanation: Marzipan is made mainly from ground almonds and sugar.

text: In Norse mythology, what is the name of the giant tree that connects the nine worlds?
explanation: Yggdrasil is the world tree linking the nine worlds of Norse myth.

text: In Greek mythology, who was condemned to roll a boulder up a hill for eternity?
explanation: Sisyphus was doomed to push a boulder uphill forever, only for it to roll back down.

text: Who created the international constructed language Esperanto?
explanation: L. L. Zamenhof published Esperanto in 1887.

text: Which script is used to write the Russian language?
explanation: Russian is written in the Cyrillic script.

text: In which year was the first Harry Potter book published?
explanation: "Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone" was first published in 1997.

text: Which company created the video game character Sonic the Hedgehog?
explanation: Sonic the Hedgehog was created by Sega in 1991.

text: What is the smallest perfect number, equal to the sum of its proper divisors?
explanation: 6 is the smallest perfect number, since 1 + 2 + 3 = 6.

text: How many zeros follow the 1 in a googol?
explanation: A googol is 10 to the power of 100: a 1 followed by 100 zeros.

text: Which city was the capital of the Inca Empire?
explanation: Cusco, in present-day Peru, was the capital of the Inca Empire.

text: Most of the Great Wall of China that survives today was built under which dynasty?
explanation: The best-preserved sections of the Great Wall were built during the Ming dynasty.

text: Which strait separates Asia from North America?
explanation: The Bering Strait lies between Russia's Chukotka and Alaska.

text: Lake Titicaca lies on the border between Peru and which other country?
explanation: Lake Titicaca is shared by Peru and Bolivia.

text: Which astronomer formulated the three laws of planetary motion?
explanation: Johannes Kepler published his laws of planetary motion between 1609 and 1619.

text: Which element is the most abundant in Earth's crust by mass?
explanation: Oxygen makes up about 46% of Earth's crust by mass.

text: Which land mammal has the longest pregnancy, lasting about 22 months?
explanation: Elephants carry their young for about 22 months, the longest of any land mammal.

text: The axolotl, a salamander that keeps its larval features as an adult, is native to which country?
explanation: The axolotl is native to the lake system of the Valley of Mexico.

text: Which poet wrote the Persian epic "Shahnameh" (The Book of Kings)?
explanation: The "Shahnameh" was written by the poet Ferdowsi around the year 1010.

text: Miguel de Cervantes and William Shakespeare both died in which year?
explanation: Both Cervantes and Shakespeare died in 1616.

text: Which painter created the triptych "The Garden of Earthly Delights"?
explanation: "The Garden of Earthly Delights" was painted by Hieronymus Bosch.

text: Which Japanese artist created the woodblock print "The Great Wave off Kanagawa"?
explanation: "The Great Wave off Kanagawa" is a print by Katsushika Hokusai.

text: Which composer wrote the ballet "The Rite of Spring", which premiered in Paris in 1913?
explanation: "The Rite of Spring" was composed by Igor Stravinsky.

text: How many symphonies are numbered in the traditional catalog of Mozart's works?
explanation: Mozart's symphonies are traditionally numbered from 1 to 41.

text: Which film won the very first Academy Award for Best Picture?
explanation: "Wings" won the top award at the first Academy Awards in 1929.

text: Who directed the 1927 silent science-fiction film "Metropolis"?
explanation: "Metropolis" was directed by Fritz Lang.

text: In which year was the first FIFA World Cup held?
explanation: The first FIFA World Cup was held in Uruguay in 1930.

text: Which country hosted the first Winter Olympic Games in 1924?
explanation: The first Winter Olympics were held in Chamonix, France, in 1924.

text: In which year did Ray Tomlinson send the first email between computers using the @ sign?
explanation: Ray Tomlinson sent the first networked email on ARPANET in 1971.

text: What does the image format name "GIF" stand for?
explanation: GIF stands for Graphics Interchange Format, introduced in 1987.

text: Vanilla comes from the pods of a plant belonging to which plant family?
explanation: Vanilla is obtained from the seed pods of orchids of the genus Vanilla.

text: The spice known as cloves consists of which dried part of a plant?
explanation: Cloves are the dried flower buds of the clove tree.

text: In ancient Egyptian mythology, what was a dead person's heart weighed against in the afterlife?
explanation: The heart was weighed against the feather of Ma'at, the goddess of truth.

text: In Norse mythology, what is the name of Odin's eight-legged horse?
explanation: Odin rides Sleipnir, an eight-legged horse.

text: How many letters are in the modern Greek alphabet?
explanation: The Greek alphabet has 24 letters, from alpha to omega.

text: Which ancient writing system did Jean-François Champollion decipher in 1822?
explanation: Champollion deciphered Egyptian hieroglyphs using the Rosetta Stone.

text: In which year was Nintendo's original Game Boy first released in Japan?
explanation: The original Game Boy launched in Japan in April 1989.

text: Under which name was the arcade game Pac-Man originally released in Japan in 1980?
explanation: Pac-Man was first released in Japan as "Puck-Man" in 1980.
